unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: More generally than (7), we can let $\hat L:=\max\{i:R_i\le R_m^{(J)}\}$, for fixed $J$, where $R_m^{(J)}$ denotes the $J$th smallest value amongst the block averages $R_1,\ldots,R_m$. With this generalized definition we have more data to estimate the long-run variance.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original optional fixed-J order-statistic selection rule. Preserve separately from the basic argmin in (7); it does not supply an unstated tie rule for every estimator.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: The long-run variance estimate $\hat\sigma_\infty^2$ can be specified by the user. Our estimator $\hat\sigma^2$, defined in (8), is a canonical choice, but any consistent estimate can be used.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original choice allowed in blockwise statistic (9) and Theorem3.3. Theorem3.2 studies the particular estimator (8); its stronger assumptions are not automatically imposed on the global test.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Let $\mathbb B$ denote a standard Brownian motion and $\mathbb B_1(u)=\mathbb B(u)-u\mathbb B(1)$ be the Brownian bridge. For all $x\le0$, we have
\[
\mathbb P\left(\inf_{u\in[0,1]}\mathbb B_1(u)\le x\right)=e^{-2x^2};\tag{18}
\]
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original interpretation of the limiting distribution. A Brownian representation of the observed noise is not an extra assumption in Theorem3.1.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Theorem 3.1(i) suggests that, given level $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we can use the $\alpha$-quantile of the limit, $-(-0.5\log\alpha)^{1/2}$, as the cutoff value to test $H_0$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original lower-tail global cutoff, distinct from the standard-normal blockwise cutoff z_(1-1/m).

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: As a rule of thumb, we use $\rho=1/2$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Optional practical default; the original locating estimator and Theorem3.3 permit rho in (0,1), subject to gap comparability.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: In particular, we do not require that $\tau\asymp n$. The requirement $k\ll\tau$ ensures that there is an increasing number of blocks before the change. The requirement $n-\tau\ge2k$ is slightly weaker and ensures that there is at least one complete block after the change.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original explanation allowing early or late changes; do not impose a fixed interior change fraction on the localization theorem.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We show (Lemma A.5) that our proposed $\hat d$ consistently estimates $d_*$. By definition $d_*\ge d$; i. e., $d_*$ provides an upper bound for the gap $d$. The regularity condition $d>Kd_*$, for a constant $K>\rho$, requires that $d_*$, which is tractable, also facilitates a lower bound with respect to $d$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original distinction between the lower pointwise gap bound and the estimable averaged gap. The supplementary proof is not read or imported.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
If the true $d$ were known, we could use the following estimate for $\tau$:
\[
\tilde\tau:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{j=2,\ldots,n}\sum_{t=1}^{j-1}(X_t-\hat\mu_1-\rho d).\tag{21}
\]
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original oracle alternative, distinct from the actual estimator using d_hat in (12). Do not replace the main estimator by this easier known-gap procedure.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Condition 3.1 holds, for example, under the geometric moment contraction $\delta_{n,\theta}=O(\rho^n)$ for some $\rho\in(0,1)$,
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original sufficient example, not an additional geometric-decay hypothesis. This rho is a decay factor, distinct from the localization tuning parameter.

statement_local_bindings.T3.1: Common model has stationary centered causal noise with strictly positive finite long-run variance. Theorem assumes summability of L2 functional dependence. Under constant-mean H0 the minimum CUSUM statistic has the printed one-sided Brownian-bridge minimum distribution. Under the irregular one-sided H1, the signal rate forces the statistic to negative infinity in probability. Definition (5) requires a consistent variance estimate under the hypothesis being considered. It need not be estimator (8), and the stronger Condition3.1/block rates are not added as general premises.
statement_local_bindings.T3.2: This theorem studies the particular selected-prefix overlapping-block estimator sigmahat² in (8). Resolve block size/count, minimum-block index and prefix endpoint, preliminary mean, sliding block averages and the true block index eta=floor(tau/k). d,tau come from H1 and can depend onn. Condition3.1 supplies the same theta used in the d and k rate requirements. Preserve the deterministic O(1/k) and separate random O_P(eta^(2/min(4,theta)-1)) terms. No blockwise decisions or refined localization step is required.
statement_local_bindings.T3.3: Actual estimator (12) uses the improved prefix mean and estimated averaged gap, which depend on block means, preliminary index/mean, standardized block statistics, normal-quantile decisions and binary step fit. Variance estimate in (9) may be any consistent estimator, not necessarily (8). Resolve d_star using the true block index and signal means, retain d>K*d_star with K>rho and rho in(0,1), the same theta across all rates, and n-tau>=2k. The conclusion is the printed d_star^(-theta/(theta-1)) localization rate for the first changed observation.

source_issues.note: Registered arXiv2409.08863v1, stamped13September2024,39pages. Main text ends after acknowledgments/funding on16. Supplementary availability listings and references occupy17–18; appendix bodies start19 and are excluded. Exactly three main-text Theorems3.1–3.3; Corollary3.1 is not inventoried.

Tau denotes the first changed observation, so pre-change means stop at tau-1 and the final argmin sums through j-1. d is a positive lower bound for all post-change gaps, not necessarily the attained minimum. d_star averages the signal over sliding blocks; d_hat estimates that averaged quantity. Preserve the strict d>K*d_star inequality with K>rho; feasibility with d_star>=d implies K<1 rather than an arbitrary large constant.

The source defines eta=floor(tau/k) and also calls it the last fully pre-change block, writing eta*k+1<=tau<=(eta+1)*k. At tau exactly divisible byk, that interval is inconsistent and the eta-th block includes the first changed observation. Retain the literal floor definition and the contradictory prose; do not silently substitute floor((tau-1)/k).

Definitions(5) and(9) permit any consistent long-run-variance estimator; estimator(8) is a suggested canonical choice. Theorem3.2 supplies a rate for(8) under its own stronger moment/block/gap conditions. These do not become mandatory premises ofTheorem3.1, and Theorem3.3 does not require that its user-chosen variance estimate be(8). The mean muhat0 from(8) is still a required preliminary mean for(9).

R_(s/k) extends nonoverlapping R_j to sliding windows even for noninteger s/k. The variance estimate uses k/(ellhat-k+1), all endpoints s=k..ellhat and centering by the entire selected-prefix mean. It is not an average over only the original disjoint block means.

Argmin tie-breaking for L_hat, eta_hat and tau_hat is not stated. The optional fixed-J max-index selection is not a general tie convention. For finite data, eta_hat=m-1 is allowed by(10) but makes the sliding-window range in d_hat empty; no fallback is supplied. High-probability asymptotics do not by themselves define these bad finite-sample outputs.

Population long-run variance is explicitly positive and finite. Generic consistent estimates can still be zero or negative on finite-sample events; estimator(8) is nonnegative but can be zero. The source does not fully specify square-root/sign/zero-division conventions. m>=2 is needed for the interior normal quantile and step-fit range, and follows eventually from the stated growth regime.

Functional dependence replaces only innovation0 by an independent copy. Cumulative dependence sums over future indices, while long-run covariance sums over all integer lags. Condition3.1 retains both theta regimes and the exact gamma_theta radical/log threshold; gamma_theta is not the autocovariance gamma(k). The same theta must satisfy all moment, signal and block-rate conditions.

Theorem3.2 has separate deterministic and probabilistic error terms. Theorem3.3 uses d_star with negative exponent theta/(theta-1). Rho=1/2, block length ceil(n^(1/3)) and geometric moment contraction are optional examples, not universal hypotheses. Early and late changes are allowed; tau need not be proportional ton.

Brownian-bridge limits and KMT coupling interpret or prove the statistical results, not extra assumptions on observed noise. Oracle true-gap estimator(21) is not the actual estimator(12). Appendix proofs are excluded. The empirical interpretation of a search-index change as an epidemic starting date is application context and is not certified by this theorem census.

ambient_prerequisites: Real deterministic mean sequences and stationary centered processes; covariance and positive finite two-sided long-run variance.
Causal measurable processes driven by IID innovations, independent-copy coupling, Ltheta norms and summable functional-dependence tails.
Finite partial sums, integer floors and sliding windows, empirical prefix means, minimum/argmin operations and binary indicator step fitting.
Standard-normal quantiles for blockwise decisions; Brownian-bridge minimum distribution only as the global-test limiting interpretation.
Convergence in probability, little-o and stochastic O_P, deterministic versus random rate remainders and n-dependent change positions/gap sequences.

Tie, empty-window, exact block-boundary and finite-estimate division issues are recorded rather than filled with invented conventions. All statement definitions are available in main text; no appendix-only definition is needed.
validation_limits: Main-text source fidelity and dependency scope only. No proof or library-availability verdict, and no certification of empirical causal interpretations. The recorded source indexing and finite-sample definition limitations remain unresolved.
